wheel.note: Cruiser Corps lists the same 15x5.5 OEM steel wheel for 1958–1990 FJ40, FJ45, FJ55, FJ60, FJ62 and BJ trucks, and advises against tires wider than 10.5 in on it.

max_tire.note: IH8MUD's 'tried and true' answer. 33x9.50R15 fits on stock rims but rubs at the rear over bumps or at full flex; owners fix it with 1-inch bump-stop spacers and by adjusting the front steering stops.

items.title: Fuel tank separator welds can crack
items.summary: High temperature and load can pressurize the tank and crack its welds, leaking fuel, which can cause a fire near an ignition source; the remedy was an improved tank. NHTSA files it under 1980–90 Land Cruisers (38,500 vehicles), and Corsetti describes it as a 60 Series campaign, so confirm it applies to your truck.

items.title: Steering tie rod can fracture on rough roads at speed
items.summary: NHTSA lists this campaign (855 vehicles) for 1981 Land Cruisers without naming the body style, and Corsetti Cruisers describes it as an FJ60 recall: driven continuously above 50 mph on extremely rough roads, the tie rod can resonate, bend and eventually fracture. The remedy was a new tie rod and relay rod. Check with Toyota whether a 1981 FJ40 was included.

items.title: Electrical wiring campaign
items.summary: NHTSA lists a 1968–69 Land Cruiser electrical-wiring campaign covering 263 vehicles, but its online record carries no defect summary or remedy text and doesn't name the body style.

timeline.change: J40 series launched in Japan with the 3.9 L F six, a three-speed and a two-speed transfer case
Hagerty's date for the start of US FJ40 imports (Toyota's US pressroom says 1960); by 1965 the Land Cruiser is Toyota's best-selling vehicle in America
Factory roll bar becomes standard on US FJ40s
4.2 L 2F replaces the F with a four-speed; rear barn doors on US trucks
Front disc brakes, on top of the 2F and four-speed from 1975. IH8MUD members say most buyers prefer 1976-on trucks for those reasons, with 1978 the coveted year
Front door vent windows deleted; rear vent windows added to US hardtops
Optional power steering and A/C, square grille bezels, US axle ratio raised from 4.11 to 3.70 for highway cruising
End of J40 production in most markets, replaced by the 70 Series; Brazil's Bandeirante continues to 2001

identify.intro: Few FJ40s are still original: engines are swapped, bodies re-skinned and trucks titled by build date or sale date. Match the numbers before you pay for originality.

items.head: Frame number and plate
items.body: Check that the frame number on the frame matches the VIN plate. On 1960s US trucks the plate is on the firewall, later on the passenger-side fender well; an A-pillar plate appears from about 3/1969, and from about 1978 the plate is pop-riveted back on the firewall. Specter Off-Road's frame-number chart dates a truck to its build month.

items.head: Build date vs model year
items.body: The driver's door pillar is stamped with the build month. A truck built late in a year is often titled as the next model year, so quote the production date at the parts counter.

items.head: Engine numbers
items.body: The firewall plate lists the engine number. A mismatch means a replacement block. Small-block Chevy V8 swaps are very common, and on BaT swapped trucks sell for less than stock ones.

items.head: Year tells
items.body: US trucks: barn doors from 1975, front discs from 1976, vent-window changes for 1977, square grille bezels and optional power steering and A/C from 1979.

items.head: Diesels and Bandeirantes
items.body: Diesel 40s (BJ, HJ) were never sold to US retail buyers, so a US diesel is an import or an ex-mine truck. Brazilian Bandeirantes (OJ and BJ codes) look like FJ40s but used Mercedes-Benz or later Toyota 14B diesels.

values.intro: FJ40 prices have come off their 2016 peak but stay strong for original, rust-free trucks, while ICON-style restomods sit in a class of their own.
values.note: Based on 244 Bring a Trailer sales from January 2025 to October 2026 (median about $29,400). V8-swapped trucks sold for a median of about $25,300, below stock ones. ICON builds sold for $98,500–$140,000. In 2019 Hagerty put the average #2 (excellent) FJ40 at $47,375.

paragraphs: US FJ40s were all gasoline sixes. Diesel BJ40s, BJ42s and H-engine 40s, and Brazilian Bandeirantes (built to 2001), are gray-market. A vehicle at least 25 years old, measured from its date of manufacture, can be imported into the US without meeting FMVSS, so every J40-family truck now qualifies. JDMBUYSELL notes that EPA still expects the original-design engine or an EPA-certified replacement. Corsetti Cruisers warns that California may refuse to register an import without a 50-state-compliant emissions system, so plan for that before buying a BJ or HJ.

production.intro: Toyota built the J40 for nearly a quarter-century in Japan, and Brazil kept making it for 17 more years.
production.paint: Wikipedia's paint-code table includes Freeborn Red (309), Mustard Yellow (532), Sky Blue (854), Royal Blue (822) and code 681 Green, nicknamed 'John Deere Green'.
